title: The Board Risk Committee
briefing: As Director of Risk you attend the Board Risk Committee as a principal adviser. The committee chair, Dame Helen Oyelaran, wants to redesign how the committee works: agendas are full of updates, and decisions slip.
Propose how the committee should operate.

context.text: Dame Helen has said publicly that your culture report was the most useful paper the board read last year.
After the whistleblower story, the regulator has asked to see the committee's minutes for the last year.

evidence.title: Last four agendas
evidence.body: On average: 11 items, 9 'for noting', 2 'for decision'. 70% of time spent on updates. Two decisions deferred twice.

evidence.title: Committee terms of reference
evidence.body: Oversee the risk framework and appetite; review the enterprise risk profile; approve the risk appetite statement; review major incidents; satisfy itself on the independence of the risk function.

evidence.title: Reporting lines
evidence.body: The Director of Risk reports to the CFO. No private session with the committee chair is scheduled.

options.label: Decisions and appetite breaches first; one deep dive per meeting on an enterprise risk; updates taken as read with questions only
options.feedback: Time follows the committee's purpose: decide and challenge.

options.label: Add more meetings
options.feedback: More time spent on updates doesn't fix the balance.

options.label: Shorter papers, same agenda
options.feedback: Helps, but the agenda still favours noting over deciding.

questions.prompt: What do you propose on independence?

options.label: A direct reporting line to the committee chair alongside the CFO line, and a private session at each meeting
options.feedback: Standard good practice that protects the function's challenge.

options.label: Nothing: the CFO has never interfered
options.feedback: Independence is about structure, not current goodwill.

options.label: Report to the CEO instead
options.feedback: Better than the CFO for some, but without a committee line it still lacks independence.

questions.prompt: The CFO, your line manager, sees the proposal as a vote of no confidence. How do you handle it?

options.label: Speak to him first: it's about the role, not him; he stays your line manager; it protects him too when risk challenges finance decisions
options.feedback: Honest, respectful, and frames the benefit to him.

options.label: Take it to the chair without telling him
options.feedback: Confirms his fear and damages the relationship.

options.label: Drop the proposal
options.feedback: Gives up a governance principle to avoid discomfort.

questions.prompt: Which deep dive should come first?

options.label: Cold-chain integrity for pharma growth: the strategy depends on it and it deteriorated last quarter
options.feedback: Strategic weight plus a negative trend.

options.label: Whichever risk has been on the register longest
Decisions, the challenge the committee raised, and actions with owners and dates
options.feedback: Evidence that the committee oversees, not just receives.

lesson: A risk committee earns its place by deciding and challenging. Agenda design, an independent risk function, and minutes that show challenge make that real.
